answer: Remote attestation lets a verifier register an agent key only when an enclave proves it runs approved code with the expected MRENCLAVE. This binds identity to measured execution on genuine hardware: copying a VM cannot forge the proof, so multiplying identities requires access to attested physical silicon, not effortless virtual duplication. The cost raises Sybil resistance, though it is not absolute; shared hardware or compromised keys can still hollow out safeguards during the voyage, like rot hidden in cedar.
